title: Switch wallets, replay like a pro

items.text: Wallet switcher on the panel — a button sits on top of the trade panel, like Terminal's: your active paper wallet and its balance; one click lists every wallet with its balance, trades and PNL, another switches. Create a wallet right from the list. It follows the panel when you move it, and can be turned off in Paper wallets.
items.html: Wallet switcher on the panel — a button sits on top of the trade panel, like Terminal's: your active paper wallet and its balance; one click lists every wallet with its balance, trades and PNL, another switches. Create a wallet right from the list. It follows the panel when you move it, and can be turned off in Paper wallets.

items.text: Replay, rebuilt — pick the start by dragging a bar under the chart, then play at 1× to 25× or step candle by candle. Prices now travel inside each candle, your own fees apply, your TP / SL exit lines trigger on their own, and you can switch to 3m or 5m candles. Crosshair with open / high / low / close, wheel to zoom, a fills log, keyboard shortcuts (Space, →, B, S). Stop whenever you want: the score shows win rate, best trade, max drawdown and what holding would have done — and the candles you didn't see appear, faded.

title: Quick buy cannot touch a real order

items.text: Blanks now places its button on Axiom’s lists — it placed none at all. Their buy control was only recognised by Terminal’s class names and by a label ending in SOL; Axiom names nothing and writes only the amount. In « replace their button » mode, not finding it meant placing nothing and saying nothing, so the only button on the row was the site’s real one. Update before using a list on Axiom.

items.text: Our button is never placed inside their buy control — where their control has no name to grab, Blanks used to drop its button inside it. title: You can tell when you are hidden

items.text: The leaderboard says which window is empty — « nobody closed a trade in the last 24 hours », with one button to look at 7 days, 30 days or all time, instead of a blank table that looked broken.
items.html: The leaderboard says which window is empty — « nobody closed a trade in the last 24 hours », with one button to look at 7 days, 30 days or all time, instead of a blank table that looked broken.

items.text: Being off the ranking is now visible — when the switch is off, the Track tab and the Leaderboard section say it in plain words: you are hidden from the public ranking, your followers still see your trades. That switch was the reason a very active pseudo could be missing from the board.

items.text: A pseudo you add shows up at once — on a page with no token open (trenches, Pulse, your portfolio), the Tracking section of the settings only redrew when you changed tab: the trader was followed, but the list looked empty. It follows the state now, token or not.

items.text: One spelling per trader — pseudos are unique whatever the case, so Ledka and ledka are the same person; your list now always shows the spelling the account really has, and a duplicate that differed only by case is cleaned up. If your own pseudo has the wrong case, ✎ in the Track tab fixes it — people who follow you keep following you and see the correction.

items.text: Your keystrokes stay in Blanks — typing an amount or a pseudo in our panel used to reach Terminal and Axiom underneath, where the same letters are shortcuts: their app reacted while you were simply filling a field. A guard now installs itself before their page boots and keeps every key pressed inside Blanks inside Blanks. Clicks in our windows no longer reach their page either.

items.text: No more dead cursor — while a window was closing, its veil stayed clickable for a fifth of a second above their page: the pointer felt frozen and a click could land behind. A closed window never catches the mouse again.

items.text: Replay speed is real speed — the button now reads 1:1, 2×, 4×, 10× or Auto, and 1:1 means one second of chart per second: a two-second candle takes two seconds on screen. It shows the resulting length next to it, and falls back to Auto when a hold is too long to sit through.
